name: 1PhoneMirror
description: 1PhoneMirror is a Windows-based screen-mirroring receiver designed for Intune admins to capture consistent, framed mobile-device screens for documentation and training. It supports iOS/macOS AirPlay with optional PIN, Android wireless debugging via bundled adb/scrcpy, and experimental Miracast, delivering one-click screenshots or MP4/GIF recordings inside a device frame. Multiple devices can stay paired and be switched from a bottom bezel, with no app installations on phones.
author: Simon Skotheimsvik

securityCheck.aiSummary: Overall assessment: The codebase is intended for building and packaging the 1PhoneMirror MSI/Intune wrapper with Azure Trusted Signing. The primary security risk is the runtime download of the signing library without integrity checks or version pinning, which could enable supply-chain compromise. Additionally, several signing-related defaults are hardcoded and an HTTP timestamp endpoint is used, both of which should be addressed with better key management and secure endpoints. Other patterns (Intune packaging, signing flow) are normal for this tooling.

noRemoteExecution.reason: The trusted signing workflow fetches Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll from NuGet at runtime via Get-TrustedSigningDlib. There is no version pinning or integrity verification, creating a supply-chain risk and potential remote code execution if the downloaded library is compromised.
